To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cladding is heated at high rates (up to 500 K/ms) and is submitted to large strain rates (up to a few %/ms) during the PCMI phase.

the cladding tube is subjected to a thermomechanical load characterized by a heating rate of 1000 °C/s, a maximum cladding temperature of 1100 °C, an axial strain rate of 0.5 s−1 and a biaxial loading ratio close to 0.5.
the cladding tube was subjected to a very severe thermomechanical load.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to predict the cladding mechanical response to the RIA.
the study of the thermomechnical loading applied on a cladding tube during an RIA initiated at 280 °C.
the following topics: (i) the thermomechanics of the fuel rod during the PCMI phase of a RIA, (ii) the cladding mechanical properties, and (iii) the cladding fracture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cladding mechanical response and fracture are mainly driven by the strain rate and loading path.
the cladding tube is submitted during the PCMI phase to high thermomechanical loadings that could lead to cladding failure.
, for the considered RIA scenario, a significant part of the cladding tube was subjected to a very high thermomechanical load during the PCMI phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermomechanically induced fracture is the dominant failure mode for the cladding tube of the CABRI RP-Na5 pulse.
the cladding temperature and the heating rate are the most important factors that control the cladding behavior and failure mode during the PCMI phase of a RIA.
the cladding temperature is the main parameter controlling the cladding mechanical response and failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a significant amount of plastic deformation is accumulated in the cladding tube, which can lead to cladding fracture during the PCMI phase.
the cladding tube experiences a very high loading biaxially (up to 2.3) that can be responsible for a cladding fracture by the so-called ‘bending’ failure mode.
the loading conditions during the PCMI phase are very different than those usually considered in PCMI studies.
